title: Token flow minimums + live-streaming pricing probe (IO ratio discounts & streaming floor)
creator: Priya Rao
description: Background: customers frequently have asymmetric token patterns (many short inputs, large model outputs e.g., summarization; or large inputs, trimmed outputs e.g., classification). Current flat per-token pricing doesn't capture unit economics and leads to leakage where streaming sessions with long-lived connections appear cheap per-minute but expensive per-output. Goal: run a hosted pricing experiment that introduces (A) an I/O ratio discount band (if output/input > X then discounted output rate) and (B) a live-streaming floor (per-minute or per-session minimum) to better align revenue with sustained resource usage.
description_long:
Experiment scope and variants:
- Variant A1 (IO-ratio discount): Keep base rates at $0.0008/input-token and $0.0012/output-token. Apply tiered discount where output-token rate is reduced by 10% when output/input >= 3x, and 20% when >= 6x. The metric is to capture workloads like long-form generation where KV-cache reuse reduces marginal cost but network/IO is high.
- Variant A2 (Reverse): discount input-token for classification-heavy customers where input >> output to encourage embedding-like workloads.
- Variant B1 (Streaming floor): For streaming responses mark a minimum charge per active stream of $0.005/minute after first 30s, with first 30s free. Intended to cover amortized GPU slot time and connection overhead.
- Variant B2 (Session minimum): instead of per-minute floor, a per-session minimum equivalent to 2 output tokens at base rate for sessions longer than 60s.
Primary success metrics:
- Revenue per 1000 requests (containment vs control)
- Weighted RPM (revenue per minute of GPU) and revenue delta normalized to utilization
- Churn signals among top-100 paying customers (delta)
- Latency/SLO regressions or billing disputes
Secondary metrics:
- Percent of requests hitting discounts/floor
- Average tokens billed per session
- Customer support tickets referencing billing increases
Telemetry and rollout plan:
1) Instrument tagging in API billing pipeline (ENG-4210): add fields io_ratio, session_duration_seconds, streaming_active_minutes to billing event.
2) Run closed beta with 20 customers (mix of AI startups and mid-market SaaS) for 2 weeks behind opt-in flag. Monitor dashboard: grafana/redwood/billing/pm-18001.
3) If closed beta satisfies safety checks (no >2% churn signals, revenue delta >= +5% w/o significant support tickets) expand to randomized 10% of traffic for 4 weeks.
4) Full rollout contingent on legal review and contract language for enterprise customers (work with Sales/legal for opt-outs).
Billing & infra changes required:
- Billing pipeline: add conditional price calculator branch and store applied_reason tag. (ENG-4210)
acceptance_criteria: Billing pipeline emits io_ratio and session_duration_seconds for every billed event
Closed beta executed with 20 customers and no critical billing incidents
Dashboards show clear mapping from variant to revenue delta and utilization metrics
Support runbook for common dispute scenarios documented and reviewed
Legal approves language for enterprise contract and security questionnaire updates

notes: Risk: customers using long-poll streaming for low-throughput chat may see nominal increases; mitigate via first-30s free policy in B1.
Tradeoff: IO-ratio discounts add complexity to pricing docs and to explain to sales; plan 1-pager for AE enablement.
Follow-ups: if positive, evaluate adding IO-ratio as a configurable enterprise knob in Dedicated and Private deployments (project: runtime-pricing-config).
